annotatedSteps.description: Convert tan θ and cot θ into terms of sin θ and cos θ
annotatedSteps.studentWork:
LHS = tanθ/(1 − cotθ) + cotθ/(1 − tanθ)
= (sinθ/cosθ)/((sinθ − cosθ)/sinθ) + (cosθ/sinθ)/((cosθ − sinθ)/cosθ)
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: ✓ Correctly converted tan and cot to ratios of sin and cos

annotatedSteps.description: Simplify fractions, adjust sign to find common denominator, and combine
annotatedSteps.studentWork:
= sin²θ/(cosθ(sinθ − cosθ)) − cos²θ/(sinθ(sinθ − cosθ))
= (sin³θ − cos³θ)/(sinθ cosθ (sinθ − cosθ))
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: ✓ Correctly handled the negative sign change and formed the common denominator

annotatedSteps.description: Factorise numerator using a³ − b³ identity and simplify using sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 to reach RHS
annotatedSteps.studentWork:
= (sinθ − cosθ)(sin²θ + sinθ cosθ + cos²θ)/(sinθ cosθ (sinθ − cosθ))
= (1 + sinθ cosθ)/(sinθ cosθ)
= 1/(sinθ cosθ) + 1
= 1 + secθ cosecθ = RHS. Hence proved.
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: ✓ Perfectly factored and simplified to RHS with valid identities

teacherNote: Marked against: Expressing tan θ and cot θ in terms of sin θ and cos θ and simplifying denominators (1); Taking common denominator to obtain (sin³θ − cos³θ) / (sinθ cosθ (sinθ − cosθ)) (1); Applying a³ − b³ expansion and sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 to arrive at RHS (1). Excellent solution. Every step, sign adjustment, and algebraic identity was applied accurately and written out clearly.
